target_customer: Informal neighbourhood retailers in Sub-Saharan Africa, and consumer brands selling to them
problem: Small merchants struggle to source stock, pay digitally and access credit.
business_model: B2B marketplace margins and fintech services (wallet, agency banking, airtime)
product_category: B2B e-commerce and fintech for informal retail

founders.name: Mesongo Sibuti
founders.background_notes: YC page: techpreneur and software architect.

founders.name: Tesh Mbaabu
founders.background_notes: YC page: product and commercial strategist in business process automation and African startups.

competitors.name: Sokowatch
competitors.what: B2B ordering platform for informal retailers in East Africa
competitors.funding_then: TechCrunch headline $14M Series A (date not confirmed)

competitors.name: TradeDepot
competitors.what: Supply chain platform for manufacturers, distributors and retailers in Nigeria

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile ordering and wallet integrations are standard; operations, logistics and credit are the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Merchant and brand network helps but price competition from Wasoko and Twiga kept margins thin.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals raised larger rounds; MarketForce shut its marketplace in April 2024.

market_need_then: Informal retailers dominate African retail and lacked digital sourcing and credit; Series A coverage cited over 100,000 merchants in 2022.

branding.brand_signature: RejaReja merchant app (Kiswahili for retail per a secondary source)

rebrands.why: Marketplace wound down because of thin margins and price competition, per cofounder quote in press

brand_strength.rationale: Local app brand with trade press coverage, but no evidence it drove growth.

pivots.from: RejaReja B2B e-commerce for informal merchants
pivots.why: Thin margins and price competition made the marketplace unsustainable (cofounder quote via search results)

outcome_analysis: MarketForce raised a $40M equity and debt Series A in February 2022 led by V8 Capital Partners, but cut about 9% of staff in 2022 and in 2023 reportedly scaled back after some investors reneged on commitments. It exited most markets and wound down RejaReja in April 2024 over thin margins, moving to Chpter social commerce.
notes: July 2021 round: Food Business Africa calls it a $2M Series A; Techpoint calls it pre-Series A; labelled other. Series A of $40M mixes equity and debt per search snippet; fetch of the Finextra page was blocked, details taken from search results and several outlets. Competitor sources are dated July 2021, about 11 months after the batch. YC lists Active while the company exited its marketplace business; exit left none because the entity continues as Chpter. Layoff and market exit claims from TechCrunch, Techpoint and WeeTracker headlines. Site marketforce.io returned 503.
